system_description.narrative_title: Drone and Black Sea escalation in the Russia–Ukraine war
system_description.narrative_summary: A concentrated campaign of drone and missile strikes by Ukraine targeting Russian territory, ports and logistics — and retaliatory/defensive actions by Russia and NATO — is disrupting Black Sea maritime trade, straining energy and steel flows, and spilling into neighbouring airspace. NATO and regional states are increasingly intercepting suspected Russian drones, while economic and political pressures at home and abroad amplify risks of wider escalation and supply-chain shocks.
system_description.scope: Hostilities between Russia and Ukraine focused on drone/missile strikes, Black Sea maritime security and port operations, NATO and neighbouring states' air-defence responses, and the resulting economic and political impacts on energy, trade and domestic stability.
system_description.super_system: Euro-Atlantic security architecture and global trade/energy system
adjacent_subsystems: NATO military posture and regional air-defence
Black Sea maritime commerce and energy export routes
Russian domestic politics, economy and military mobilization
Western sanctions, trade policy and supply chains

variables.name: Drone strike rate
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of unmanned aerial vehicle strikes targeting assets or territory associated with the conflict per unit time.

variables.name: Missile strike rate
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of guided or ballistic missile strikes associated with the conflict per unit time.

variables.name: Air-defense interception rate
variables.description: The rate at which air-defense systems detect and successfully intercept aerial threats in the region per unit time.

variables.name: Cross-border incident rate
variables.description: The frequency of incursions, breaches, or spillover military or aerial incidents across neighbouring airspace or borders per unit time.

variables.name: Port operational capacity
variables.description: The functional capacity of regional ports to load, unload, store, and process maritime cargo and energy shipments at a point in time.

variables.name: Maritime cargo flow
variables.description: The volume of commercial goods transiting the maritime corridor associated with the theatre per unit time.

variables.name: Energy export flow
variables.description: The volume and continuity of energy (e.g., oil, refined products, gas) shipments and exports moving through regional routes per unit time.

variables.name: Steel supply flow
variables.description: The rate at which steel and related industrial inputs are produced, transported, and delivered from the region into supply chains per unit time.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premium level
variables.description: The prevailing cost and risk premium applied to maritime insurance for vessels operating in or near the affected sea routes at a point in time.

variables.name: Supply-chain delay rate
variables.description: The rate at which shipments and logistics services experience delays or disruptions attributable to the conflict per unit time.

variables.name: Domestic political stability
variables.description: The overall level of internal political cohesion, protest, governance effectiveness, and social order within involved societies at a point in time.

variables.name: Military recruitment pressure
variables.description: The demand and social/political pressure to mobilize, recruit, or conscript personnel into armed forces per unit time.

variables.name: International military support intensity
variables.description: The rate and scale of external military assistance, materiel transfers, and operational cooperation flowing into the conflict theatre per unit time.

variables.name: Attribution uncertainty
variables.description: The level of ambiguity and lack of confidence among stakeholders about who is responsible for particular attacks or incidents at a point in time.

variables.name: Electronic warfare activity
variables.description: The intensity of electromagnetic operations, jamming, and countermeasures employed to degrade sensors, communications, or control systems per unit time.

variables.name: Perceived escalation risk
variables.description: The collective perception among regional actors and publics of the likelihood that the conflict will broaden or trigger wider military confrontation at a point in time.

catalysts.title: Renewed Ukraine–Black Sea interdiction campaign
catalysts.description: Sustained Ukrainian strikes and Russian countermeasures around Black Sea ports and shipping lanes, disrupting loadings and insurance costs.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines: port attacks/halts/resumptions, Danube and Odesa/Izmail strikes (e.g. 'Russia's Black Sea...halts loadings', 'Russia targets Danube port', 'Russia hits Ukraine's Izmail and Odesa ports').

catalysts.title: Continued NATO shoot‑downs of drones over NATO airspace
catalysts.description: Ongoing interceptions and shoot‑downs of drones in Baltic and Romanian airspace by NATO and national jets, raising incident counts and perceptions.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple recent reports of NATO and Romania shooting down drones over Latvia/Romania (e.g. 'NATO aircraft shoot down drone over Latvia', 'Romania shoots down drone').

catalysts.title: Depletion of Patriot launchers/munitions
catalysts.description: Running low on Patriot launchers/rounds reduces effective air-defence coverage, likely raising successful strike rates against defended areas.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Ukraine left exposed as Patriot launchers run empty' implies reduced interception capacity and higher successful strike rates.

catalysts.title: EU's planned autumn sanctions package
catalysts.description: A broad EU sanctions package expected in autumn that will affect Russian exports, trade flows and insurance costs in the region.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'EU plans most far-reaching sanctions package against Russia in autumn' — implies export and trade disruptions.

catalysts.title: Sustained Ukrainian drone strikes on Moscow and logistics
catalysts.description: Continued Ukrainian drone and strike operations targeting Moscow region and Russian logistics nodes, likely to persist near‑term.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Ukraine presses drone attacks on Moscow and Russian logistics', 'Ukrainian drones strike Moscow region, killing one'.

catalysts.title: Intermittent halts and resumptions at Russian Black Sea ports
catalysts.description: Cycle of drone/strike incidents causing temporary halts and resumptions of oil/commodity loadings at Black Sea terminals.
catalysts.rationale: Reports of Sheskharis halting loadings and Novorossiysk resuming after drone attacks ('Sheskharis terminal halts loadings', 'Novorossiysk port resumes oil loadings').

catalysts.title: Possible uptick in international military support after exercises
catalysts.description: Demonstrations of Ukrainian drone effectiveness and close US‑Ukraine exercises may trigger stepped-up materiel, training, or cooperation.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: US‑Ukraine exercises and Ukrainian drone performance ('Ukrainian Drone Units Handily Beat U.S.', 'U.S. and Ukrainian Forces...exercise').
